te: Special economic zone transport modelled on the EEC, preventing corruption in public procurement, and preparing the SME CONNECT seminar
se: Meeting on Thursday 19 November 2026 at 13.00, Committee Meeting Room CB 311 (Senate), Floor 3, Parliament House, according to the meeting agenda: the subcommittee studied using the transport and logistics management of the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) as a model for transport in Thailand's special economic zones, inviting representatives of the Office of Transport and Traffic Policy and Planning and of the Eastern Special Development Zone Policy Committee to give information; considered ways to prevent corruption in public procurement and subcontracting; and discussed a study visit to Kanchanaburi Province (27–28 November 2026) and the seminar “SME CONNECT 2027: Unlocking Thai SMEs, Linking the Government Market to Business Opportunities”. A summary will be added after the Senate publishes it.
it: Using the transport and logistics system of the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) as a model for special economic zones
Ways to prevent corruption in public procurement and subcontracting, so that SMEs can reach the government market transparently
Study visit to Kanchanaburi Province (27–28 November 2026)
Seminar “SME CONNECT 2027: Unlocking Thai SMEs, Linking the Government Market to Business Opportunities”

te: Pre-meeting video · Special economic zone transport modelled on the EEC, preventing corruption in public procurement, and preparing the SME CONNECT seminar
Hearing ways to prevent corruption in public procurement, so SMEs get a fair chance
se: The subcommittee invited representatives of a private-sector anti-corruption organization to give information. The representatives said that existing tools, such as the Integrity Pact and the CoST project, have improved transparency to some degree, but that gaps remain, such as bidder qualifications that limit competition, the use of scoring systems, splitting contracts into amounts below the thresholds, and sub-contracting through several layers, which make it hard for SMEs to win government work. The recommendations received were: disclosing the true shareholders of government suppliers, automatic blacklisting of contractors who abandon work, checking suppliers' readiness before they may bid, making the e-GP and e-Marketplace systems easier to use, and linking tax data so that SMEs are warned in advance. The subcommittee chair thanked the representatives for kindly giving information, and the subcommittee will use the information and recommendations in preparing its study report.
it: Information from representatives of a private-sector anti-corruption organization on tools for preventing corruption in public procurement, and the gaps that should be improved

Recommendations: disclose true shareholders, blacklist contractors who abandon work automatically, check suppliers' readiness, improve the e-GP and e-Marketplace systems, and link tax data to warn SMEs

Meeting 14/2569 · Subcommittee on Promoting SMEs and Special Economic Zones in Government and Online Markets
Fewer duplicate documents for SMEs: the new facilitation law and linking government data
se: The subcommittee studied ways to reduce the obstacles SMEs face in using government services, and invited representatives of the Office of the Public Sector Development Commission (OPDC) and the Digital Government Development Agency (DGA) to give information. The representatives said that the Licensing Facilitation and Public Service Act B.E. 2569 (2026) will come into force on 4 January 2027. It covers every type of government service; agencies must publish citizen manuals on the central info.go.th system and set out clearly how officials use their discretion; some licences can be renewed by paying the fee first, with checks afterwards; and procedures must be reviewed at least every 3 years. Earlier cooperation led 22 agencies to stop asking for copies of 3 company documents, which an assessment by the Thai Chamber of Commerce found saves more than 7,100 million baht a year. DGA explained the Government Data Exchange (GDX), why businesses still have to submit duplicate copies, and the plan to link 58 key datasets under the Cabinet resolution of 15 September 2026. The subcommittee repeated its recommendation that the government publish procurement data in machine-readable form, following the international OCDS standard at every stage. The subcommittee chair thanked the representatives for kindly giving explanations, and the subcommittee will use the information and recommendations in preparing its study report.
it: Licensing Facilitation and Public Service Act B.E. 2569 (2026), in force from 4 January 2027
Linking government data through GDX so that businesses no longer need to submit copies of documents
Repeated recommendation to publish government procurement data in machine-readable form under the OCDS standard

te: Meeting summary video · Fewer duplicate documents for SMEs: the new facilitation law and linking government data
Ways to bring SMEs into online trade and make Thai platforms more competitive
se: The subcommittee studied ways to bring SMEs into online trade and heard information from the agencies concerned. The Department of International Trade Promotion said that the Thaitrade.com website has run for about 14 years with more than 250,000 members in total, and that 58 overseas trade offices help introduce foreign buyers, along with services for SMEs such as digital skills training, roadshows in large provinces and online business matching. The meeting also heard that Thailand's e-commerce value in 2024 was about 6.13 trillion baht according to an ETDA survey, but that Thai platforms still face limits: most consumers are on foreign platforms, features consumers are used to such as live-stream selling, instalment payment and cash on delivery are lacking, each platform's strengths are scattered, and the law does not allow the state to run businesses that compete with the private sector unless necessary. The subcommittee chair thanked the agency representatives for kindly giving explanations, and the subcommittee will use the information and recommendations in preparing its study report.
it: Information from the Department of International Trade Promotion on the Thaitrade.com website and its services helping SMEs sell online
The state of online trade in Thailand and the limits of Thai platforms
